step1.title: Project Details
step1.subtitle: Let's start with the basics
step1.industryRequired: Please select or specify an industry
step1.descriptionPlaceholder: AI-powered HR platform for SMBs to automate hiring and onboarding
step1.tip: Tip: You can save draft and come back anytime

step2.title: Value Proposition
step2.subtitle: Define your unique value
step2.problemPlaceholder: Describe the specific pain point your customers face...
step2.solutionPlaceholder: Describe what your product does and how it solves the problem...
step2.solutionUniquenessPlaceholder: What makes your product fundamentally different...
step2.advantagesPlaceholder: Enter an advantage and click Add
step2.tip: Tip: Be specific with numbers and metrics. Investors value quantifiable results.

problemGuidelines.1: Describe the specific customer pain point
problemGuidelines.2: How often does this problem occur?
problemGuidelines.3: How much time/money do customers lose?
problemGuidelines.4: How do customers solve this problem now?

step2.problemExample: Example: "Startup founders spend 100+ hours creating business plans and pitch decks, not knowing if they're ready for investor meetings. 80% get rejected due to obvious gaps that could have been fixed in advance."

solutionGuidelines.1: What exactly does your product do?
solutionGuidelines.2: How does it solve the problem?

step2.solutionExample: Example: "AI-powered platform that analyzes your business model, identifies weak points, and generates investor-ready pitch deck in 15 minutes. Includes 6 specialized AI experts for different aspects: market analysis, financials, competition, risks, etc."

solutionUniquenessGuidelines.1: What makes your product fundamentally different?
solutionUniquenessGuidelines.2: Why can't customers achieve the same result in another way?
solutionUniquenessGuidelines.3: Do you have a technological advantage, data, network, or other protection from copying?

step2.solutionUniquenessExample: Example: "We use a system of 6 AI experts (not just one GPT prompt), each with specialization. Our database includes 1000+ analyzed startups, allowing us to provide industry benchmarks."
step2.advantagesExample: Example: "Analysis in 30 seconds instead of 2 weeks with consultants" • "Price €99 instead of €5,000 for consulting" • "Specific growth plan with steps, not general advice"
step2.measurableValueExample: Example: "Save 100 hours of founder's time (€5,000 equivalent). Increase funding probability from 5% to 25%. Reduce time to funding by 3 months."

step3.title: Customer Segments
step3.subtitle: Define your target audience
step3.tip: Tip: Investors want to see market validation. Include specific numbers from your research.
step3.geographyPlaceholder: Focus on UK first (English, 15K target companies)...
step3.customerValidationPlaceholder: Conducted 80 interviews with HR managers. 70% said they'd pay €50-150/mo for this...

primarySegmentGuidelines.3: Firmographics (company size, industry, role) for B2B

step3.primarySegmentExample: Example: "Pre-seed and seed stage founders of tech startups (SaaS, marketplace, fintech), seeking €200K-€2M investments. Age 28-45. Location: Europe and English-speaking countries."
step3.marketSizeExample: Example: TAM: €500M (500,000 early-stage startups globally × €1,000 average check) • SAM: €100M (European tech startup market) • SOM: €10M (10,000 clients × €99/month × 10 months in first year)

geographyGuidelines.1: Which countries/regions are your customers in?
geographyGuidelines.4: Which regions are priority at launch?

step3.geographyExample: Example: "Focus on Europe (UK, Germany, France, Netherlands) due to high startup density. English is sufficient for 70% of market. Localization to German and French planned for Year 2."

willingnessToPayGuidelines.2: Do you have Letters of Intent (LOI)?
willingnessToPayGuidelines.4: What average check is customer ready to pay?

step3.willingnessToPayExample: Example: "Conducted 100 interviews with founders. 65% ready to pay €50-150 for analysis. Launched landing page: 500 registrations, 50 prepayments at €99. Average LTV: €1,188 (12 months × €99)."

step4.title: Sales & Marketing Channels
step4.subtitle: Define your customer acquisition strategy
step4.cacBreakdownPlaceholder: Describe your CAC calculation: Google Ads €30, Content €15, Referrals €10...
step4.marketingToolsPlaceholder: List marketing tools you plan to use...
step4.marketingFunnelPlaceholder: Describe your marketing funnel with conversions...
step4.tip: Tip: Investors want to see clear acquisition strategy with realistic numbers.

acquisitionChannelsGuidelines.2: Which channel will you test first?
acquisitionChannelsGuidelines.3: Do you have experience/results with these channels?

step4.acquisitionChannelsExamples: Examples: Paid ads (Google, Facebook, LinkedIn) • SEO/content marketing • Social media • Email marketing • Partnerships/affiliates • Direct sales (outbound) • Referral program • Community (forums, groups)
step4.acquisitionChannelsExample: Example: "Product Hunt (launch), Indie Hackers (community), Y Combinator network (partnership), LinkedIn outreach (outbound), SEO blog (long-term), startup podcasts (PR)."
step4.salesChannelExample: Example: "Self-serve via Stripe checkout for €99/month plan. Founder-led sales for annual €999 plan (cold outreach + demo). Plan to hire VP Sales at €10K MRR."

cacGuidelines.1: CAC Value: total cost to acquire one customer
cacGuidelines.4: If not - provide forecast with reasoning
cacGuidelines.5: Formula: CAC = Marketing & Sales costs / New customers

step4.cacExample: Example: "CAC: €55. Breakdown: Google Ads €30/customer (CPC €2, conversion 6.7%), Content Marketing €15/customer (SEO + blog), Referral program €10/customer (20% commission)."
step4.marketingToolsExample: Example: "PostHog for analytics, ConvertKit for email (newsletter), Buffer for social media, Notion for content calendar. Budget: €200/month on tools."
step4.marketingFunnelExample: Example: "Landing page → Free tool (lite) → Trial (full) → Paid. 100% → 5% signup → 30% trial → 25% paid (1000 visitors → 50 signups → 15 trials → 4 customers). Bottleneck: signup conversion. Improvement plan: add social proof, video demo."

step5.title: Revenue & Cost Structure
step5.subtitle: Define your financial model
step5.revenuePricingPlaceholder: Describe your pricing model, tiers, and strategy...
step5.costBreakdownPlaceholder: Break down your monthly/annual costs by category...
step5.tip: Tip: Investors prioritize clear unit economics and realistic path to profitability.

revenueStreamsGuidelines.2: Percentage of total revenue for each

step5.revenueStreamsExample: Example: "Subscription (80%): €99/mo per company. Setup fees (15%): €500 one-time. Consulting (5%): €150/hr for custom integrations."
step5.revenuePricingExample: Example: "Tiered subscription: Starter €49/mo (5 users, basic features), Pro €99/mo (20 users, advanced analytics), Enterprise €299/mo (unlimited, custom integrations, dedicated support). Value-based pricing: customers save €500/mo in HR time, so €99 is 5x ROI."
step5.costBreakdownExample: Example: "Monthly costs: Founders salary €3,000 (€1,500 × 2), Developer €2,000 (contractor), OpenAI API €500 (variable), Hosting €200, Marketing €1,000, SaaS tools €200, Legal/Admin €300. Total burn: €7,200/month."

unitEconomicsGuidelines.4: Contribution Margin = Revenue per customer - COGS
unitEconomicsGuidelines.5: LTV = ARPU × Customer Lifetime × Gross Margin

step5.unitEconomicsExample: Example: "Gross Margin: 85%, ARPU: €99/month, Lifetime: 18 months, Contribution: €84. LTV: €1,505 (€99 × 18 × 0.85)."

fundingRunwayGuidelines.1: Amount Raised: total funding received to date
fundingRunwayGuidelines.2: Funding Sources: add each source with type and amount
fundingRunwayGuidelines.3: Amount Seeking: target for next funding round
fundingRunwayGuidelines.4: Use of Funds: detailed allocation plan
fundingRunwayGuidelines.5: Runway: enter your calculated runway in months

step5.fundingRunwayExample: Example: "Sources: Bootstrapped €50K, Angel €25K. Seeking: €300K. Use: €150K runway, €80K hiring, €40K marketing, €30K buffer. Runway: 11 months."

step6.title: Team
step6.subtitle: Describe your team and expertise
step6.founderExperiencePlaceholder: Describe previous startups, industry experience, skills...
step6.specialistsPlaceholder: Do you have marketing, financial, product, sales experts?
step6.gapsPlaceholder: What's missing? How will you fill gaps? When? Budget?
step6.tip: Tip: Investors invest in teams. Show relevant experience and clear hiring plan.
step6.keyRolesExample: Example: "Founders (2): John Doe, CEO (full-time): 10 years in startup consulting, MBA, first startup. Jane Smith, CTO (full-time): 8 years senior engineer at Google, first startup. Team: 1 full-stack developer (contractor, part-time), 1 designer (freelancer, as needed). Total: 2 full-time + 2 part-time."
step6.founderExperienceExample: Example: "CEO: consulted 50+ startups, helped raise €10M for clients, but never launched own startup. CTO: shipped 5 products at Google with millions of users, no startup experience. Both first-time founding team."
step6.specialistsExample: Example: "No in-house experts. Have advisors: 1) VC partner from Sequoia (fundraising strategy, 2h/month), 2) ex-CMO of SaaS unicorn (growth advice, 1h/month). Plan to hire VP Sales at month 6 when reaching €10K MRR."

gapsGuidelines.2: How do you plan to close the gap?
gapsGuidelines.3: When do you plan to hire?

step6.gapsExample: Example: "Critical gaps: 1) VP Sales (HIGH priority, hire month 6, budget €60K/year + equity), 2) Growth marketer (MEDIUM, month 9, €45K/year), 3) Customer success (LOW, month 12, €35K/year). Interim: Founders handle sales/marketing first 6 months."

step7.title: Key Resources & Activities
step7.subtitle: Describe your assets, infrastructure, and key business activities
step7.neededPlaceholder: What's critical for launch? Cost? Timeline?
step7.techStackPlaceholder: Stack, cloud provider, infrastructure, scalability, security...
step7.productionPlaceholder: How do you build and deliver your product?
step7.innovationPlaceholder: How do you research and develop new features?
step7.platformPlaceholder: How do you maintain your technical infrastructure?
step7.marketingPlaceholder: How do you attract and retain customers?
step7.operationsPlaceholder: How do you handle daily operations?
step7.name: Name
step7.tip: Tip: Show you have key resources, mitigation plans for dependencies, clear operational processes, and strategic partnerships.

existingGuidelines.2: Intellectual: Patents, trademarks? Proprietary tech? Databases? Algorithms?

step7.existingExample: Example: "Physical: Remote team, no office. Macbooks for founders. Intellectual: Proprietary AI prompts (6 expert system), database 1,000+ analyzed startups, trademark application filed. Human: 2 founders, 1 contractor, 2 advisors, network 500+ YC alumni. Financial: €50K cash, no debt."

neededGuidelines.1: What resources are critical for launch?

step7.neededExample: Example: "Need: 1) GPT-4 API access (have it), 2) Legal entity setup (€2K, 2 weeks), 3) Payment processing (Stripe, €0 setup), 4) Domain + branding (€500, done). Total: €2,500 one-time."
step7.techStackExample: Example: "Next.js 14 + TypeScript, Supabase (Postgres), Vercel hosting, OpenAI API. Fully cloud-based, auto-scaling. SOC2 compliance via Supabase. Can scale to 100K users without rewriting."

dependenciesGuidelines.1: Who are you critically dependent on?
dependenciesGuidelines.2: What if they raise prices or leave?

step7.dependenciesExample: Example: "Critical dependency on OpenAI API. Risk: 2-3x price increase. Mitigation: 1) Testing Claude/Gemini as fallback, 2) Building own fine-tuned models, 3) 50% gross margin provides buffer."

keyActivitiesGuidelines.innovation: Innovation: User research, feature prioritization, A/B testing
keyActivitiesGuidelines.marketing: Marketing: Content creation, SEO, paid ads, email campaigns
keyActivitiesGuidelines.operations: Operations: Customer support, onboarding, billing, compliance

keyActivitiesExamples.production: Production: "2-week sprints, CI/CD via GitHub Actions, 80% test coverage"
keyActivitiesExamples.innovation: Innovation: "Monthly user interviews, quarterly roadmap planning"
keyActivitiesExamples.platform: Platform: "24/7 monitoring via Datadog, auto-scaling on AWS"
keyActivitiesExamples.marketing: Marketing: "2 blog posts/week, LinkedIn daily, €500/mo Google Ads"
keyActivitiesExamples.operations: Operations: "Email support 24h SLA, automated onboarding, GDPR compliant"

step7.keyPartnersExample: Example: "Technology: Stripe (payment processing, critical). Distribution: AWS Marketplace (sales channel, 20% of leads). Strategic: HubSpot (integration partner, co-marketing, access to 100K customers)."

step8.title: Competition
step8.subtitle: Analyze your competitive landscape
step8.directCompetitorsPlaceholder: List 3-5 direct competitors with strengths, weaknesses, size...
step8.indirectCompetitorsPlaceholder: What else can customers use instead of you?
step8.whyChooseYouPlaceholder: Your unique advantage, price/value, speed, quality...
step8.defensibilityPlaceholder: What prevents competitors from copying you?
step8.tip: Tip: Show clear differentiation and sustainable competitive advantages.
step8.directCompetitorsExample: Example: "1. Carta (YC W11, $7.4B valuation) - Strengths: Brand, cap table management. Weaknesses: Complex, expensive ($2K+/year), not for pre-seed. 2. Pulley ($40M raised) - Strengths: Modern UI, simpler than Carta. Weaknesses: Focus on cap table, no AI analysis."

indirectCompetitorsGuidelines.1: What else can customers use instead?

step8.indirectCompetitorsExample: Example: "Indirect: 1) Business plan templates (Bplans.com - free but time-consuming), 2) Startup consultants (€5K-20K, slow), 3) Accelerators (free but need to pass selection), 4) Just guessing (free, risky)."
step8.whyChooseYouExample: Example: "Choose us because: 1) AI-powered in 30 sec vs 2 weeks consultants, 2) €99 vs €5,000 consulting vs €2,000 Carta, 3) Concrete action plan vs generic templates, 4) 6 expert perspectives vs single opinion, 5) Industry benchmarks (1000+ startups data). Positioning: 'Carta for pre-seed startups'."
step8.defensibilityExample: Example: "Protection: 1) Proprietary dataset (1000+ analyses, growing daily), 2) Expert prompt engineering (6 months R&D), 3) First-mover in pre-seed segment, 4) Community (founders helping founders), 5) Integration partnerships (accelerators). Window: 12-18 months before copying."

step9.title: Risks
step9.subtitle: Identify and mitigate key risks
step9.tip: Tip: Investors want to see you've thought through risks and have concrete mitigation plans.

technical.label: 8.1. Technical risks
technical.placeholder: Tech stack feasibility, API dependencies, technical debt, security...

financial.label: 8.2. Financial risks
financial.placeholder: Runway, burn rate, revenue assumptions, funding risk...

legal.label: 8.3. Legal/regulatory risks
legal.placeholder: Licensing, GDPR, third-party ToS, IP issues...

market.label: 8.4. Market risks
market.placeholder: Competition, timing, adoption barriers, economic downturn...

team.label: 8.5. Team risks
team.placeholder: Founder conflicts, key person dependency, hiring, burnout...

technical.1: Can you build with current tech stack?

examples.technical: Risks: 1) OpenAI API instability (mitigation: Claude fallback), 2) Scaling at >10K users (mitigation: async processing + Redis cache), 3) Data privacy for EU (mitigation: GDPR-compliant Supabase), 4) Prompt injection attacks (mitigation: input sanitization).
examples.financial: Risks: 1) 7-month runway (critical!) - mitigation: raise €200K seed in 3 months, 2) OpenAI costs grow faster than expected - mitigation: optimize prompts, cap usage per user, 3) Customers churn faster - mitigation: improve onboarding, add value.
examples.legal: Risks: 1) OpenAI ToS prohibits competitive products (checked - OK for tools), 2) GDPR compliance for EU customers (solved via Supabase EU hosting), 3) Giving financial advice without license (disclaimer: educational purposes only), 4) Customer data security (mitigation: encryption, SOC2).
examples.market: Risks: 1) Big players (Carta, YC) may launch similar product (mitigation: speed, niche focus), 2) VC funding winter = fewer customers (mitigation: profitable unit economics), 3) AI hype fades (mitigation: real value, not just AI buzzword), 4) Startups close in recession (mitigation: diversify to SMB).
examples.team: Risks: 1) Co-founder conflict (mitigation: 4-year vesting, clear roles), 2) CEO knows everything (mitigation: documentation, processes), 3) Can't hire VP Sales (mitigation: founder-led sales until €20K MRR), 4) Burnout (mitigation: sustainable pace, no weekends).
examples.mitigation: Risk reduction plan Q1 2026: 1) Raise €200K seed (Jan-Mar, high priority), 2) Hire contractor for backup development (Feb, €3K/month), 3) Launch Claude integration (Mar, 40h dev time), 4) Build customer success process for retention (Jan, 20h), 5) Legal ToS review (Jan, €1K).

step10.title: Growth Forecast
step10.subtitle: Define your scaling strategy and targets
step10.tractionPlaceholder: Current users/customers, revenue, growth metrics, key achievements...
step10.scalingPlanPlaceholder: Growth strategy, scaling channels, international expansion, new products...
step10.newMarketsPlaceholder: Adjacent markets, different segments, geographic expansion, product extensions...
step10.paybackPeriodPlaceholder: When break-even? When ROI for investors? IRR?
step10.targets24MonthsPlaceholder: 600 customers, €60K MRR, 12 team, profitable (20% margin), 2% SAM...
step10.tip: Tip: Show ambitious but realistic growth targets with clear path to profitability.

tractionExamples.b2b: "120 paying customers, €11.8K MRR, +25% MoM growth for last 3 months, 3.5% monthly churn, NPS 65, CAC payback 4.2 months"
tractionExamples.marketplace: "€45K GMV/month, 320 active buyers, 45 active sellers, 15% take rate, 40% repeat purchase rate, 3x growth in last quarter"
tractionExamples.preRevenue: "2,500 signups, 80 customer interviews completed, 5 pilot customers using for free (3 ready to pay), 12 LOIs worth €1,200 MRR potential"

step10.scalingPlanExample: Example: "Months 1-6: Product-led growth (freemium model, viral referral 20% discount, SEO 50 blog posts). Months 7-12: Sales-assisted (hire VP Sales, outbound to YC/Techstars, accelerator partnerships). Year 2: International expansion (German/French localization, US market via YC network)."
step10.newMarketsExample: Example: "Year 1: European pre-seed startups. Year 2: US market (500K startups), Seed/Series A stage ($199/month plan). Year 3: SMB market (brick-and-mortar businesses), White-label for banks/accelerators (B2B2C model)."

paybackPeriodGuidelines.2: When will you return invested capital?

step10.paybackPeriodExample: Example: "Break-even: month 18 (85 customers, €8.4K MRR). Payback period for €200K seed: month 30 (at 30% net margin, €6K profit/month after break-even). Projected IRR for seed investors: 35% annually with exit at Year 5 at €50M valuation."

targetsExamples.12mo: Example 12mo: "150 customers, €15K MRR (€180K ARR), 5 team, break-even: NO, 0.5% SAM"
targetsExamples.24mo: Example 24mo: "600 customers, €60K MRR (€720K ARR), 12 team, profitable (20% margin), 2% SAM, Series A €1.5M"
targetsExamples.36mo: Example 36mo: "2,000 customers, €200K MRR (€2.4M ARR), 25 team, 30% margin (€720K profit/year), 5% SAM"
